title: The second vector on the pair of solutions, and the co-distance-3 cancellation
claim: At n = 2^m, h = n/2, for a in GF(2n)* with G = Q(Y) + k P(Y) the monic least polynomial, k = h - deg G, J = ceil(k/2), N = G(k) G(k + 1) and L(Y) = Y + Y^2 + ... + Y^(h/2): (1) for k >= 2, [Y^d](N L) = 0 for h - k + 1 <= d <= h - 2 and [Y^(h-1)](N L) = a^2 G(0)^2 (the second-order solvability in its plainest form); (2) for x = G Y^i, y = G Y^j with 2i, 2j < k - 1 and i + j <= k - 3, the reduction's order-4 coefficient (complement containing k G Y^j) is Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + Q4 + Q5 with Q1 = [k^(h-2)](Y^j W_x) = 0 and Q2 = [Y^(h-2-j)] W_x = 0 (the gap, and a double sum over powers of two collapsing), Q3 = [k^(h-2)](Y^j I_x), I_x = G tau phi_2 + k W_x, Q4 = a^2 phi_2(0) y(0), Q5 = B_4(x, y), for any second chain vector phi_2; (3) psi_hat_x = R_x + k (W_x + P R_x)/Q, R_x = (W_x Q'') mod Q (P Q'' + Q P'' = 1), is a second chain vector whenever its degree is below h. Computed: Q3 + Q4 + Q5 = 0 for psi_hat_x at every pair (sides 16 to 64), so the order-4 coefficient vanishes there; a first continued-fraction reading does not show the leading form. The registered target, the co-distance-3 cancellation, is not derived (the remaining identity concerns the high coefficients of a quotient by Q; the order-5 coefficient was not reduced), so by the frozen stop rule the collapse line is parked.
failure_conditions: An eigenvalue and an entry with i + j <= k - 3 at which the reduction's coefficient at l^4 or l^5 is nonzero (computed false at every a for sides 8 to 256).
foundation_claim_scope: The square torus of rule-60 rings with equally spaced law-(12, 12) contacts, cut open by a ring of cuts each way (A30, A32, A37, A38); its walk over GF(2), at sides 2^m. The spectrum is a contact-level reading, so it does not depend on how the rings are declared (A45).
